claims.claim: When invoking project-structure, select its private references according to the task rather than reading all of them by default.
claims.trigger: Project-structure workflow loaded; reference selection before implementation
claims.exceptions: Both references may be relevant to a task; the restriction is on automatic indiscriminate loading.
claims.enforcement_effect: Procedural context-loading instruction, not an executable block

baseline_comparisons.reason: Primary labels IMPLEMENTATION and replica NON_NORMATIVE; neither registers the negative bulk-loading default.

Reading applicable governing rules before greenfield changes does not forbid reading unnecessary private references. Private-reference ownership/existence checking controls citation, not task-selective loading.

claims.comparison_reason: Three-run claims and relevant dismissed ranges contain governing-rule reading and private-reference ownership, but no independently registered restriction on default bulk loading of this workflow's references.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: For a frontend-only placement task, read all applicable governing rules and solution-layout, then automatically load backend-layout despite no backend scope. The existing rule-reading and private-ownership claims are satisfied while the source selection default is violated.

claims.claim: A headless architecture-decision run must not wait for a decision response.
claims.trigger: Autonomous/headless run with an unresolved Reserved decision
claims.exceptions: Source distinguishes continuing compliant work from making the Reserved decision; no waiting exception stated.
claims.enforcement_effect: Procedural instruction; no runtime enforcement asserted

baseline_comparisons.reason: Both require proceeding only with compliant non-Reserved work and reporting unresolved decisions. They omit the explicit no-wait phrase, but proceeding could semantically imply it; source quote inclusion alone does not settle registration.
This concerns already-approved headless Reserved work, not waiting for unapproved choices.

claims.comparison_reason: The timing prohibition may be independent when there is no compliant work left, but equivalence to existing proceed/report claims remains plausible.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A headless run has no non-Reserved work left, makes no Reserved decision, but waits for approval before issuing its final unresolved report. Whether prior proceed/report claims already forbid this is unresolved.
claims.open_question: Does mandatory proceed/report already entail no waiting, including when Proceeding with is nothing?
